questions.question: A chemist performs chromatography on a sample of food dye and observes a single spot that has travelled up the paper. What can they conclude about the dye sample?
options: It is a pure substance because it did not separate into multiple spots.
It is a mixture because it travelled up the paper with the solvent.
It is insoluble because it only formed a single spot.
It is a mixture of two dyes that have the same chemical formula.

questions.question: An unknown poison needs to be identified from a forensic sample. Chromatograms of four known reference toxins (A, B, C, and D) and the unknown sample are run under identical conditions. How can the unknown toxin be identified?
options: By finding which reference toxin has spots that align horizontally at the same height as the spot(s) from the unknown.
By choosing the reference toxin that produces the largest number of total spots.
By finding which reference toxin travels the furthest distance regardless of the unknown's position.
By choosing the reference toxin that is most soluble in the chromatography paper itself.

questions.question: During a chromatography experiment, a student mistakenly draws the start line with a black ink pen instead of a pencil. What is the most likely consequence of this mistake when the chromatogram is developed in water?
options: The ink from the pen will dissolve and separate, interfering with the sample spots.
The ink from the pen will remain fixed at the bottom while the pencil line would have dissolved.
The solvent will be blocked by the ink and will not be able to rise up the paper.
The sample spots will react chemically with the ink and change color.

questions.question: A chemical plant needs to separate a mixture containing water (boiling point 100°C), ethanol (78°C), propanol (97°C), and butanol (117°C). Which technique is most appropriate for this task and why?
options: Fractional distillation, because there are more than two components with some having close boiling points.
Simple distillation, because all four liquids have different boiling points.
Filtration, because the different liquids have different particle sizes.
Evaporation, because the lighter liquids will evaporate and leave the heaviest liquid behind.

questions.question: During a simple distillation experiment, the flow of cold water through the outer jacket of the Liebig condenser is accidentally cut off, causing the condenser to warm up. What will be the direct consequence of this issue?
options: The condenser becomes less effective, allowing more gaseous product to escape into the air.
The boiling point of the liquid in the distillation flask will increase.
The distillate collected in the receiving flask will contain more solid impurities.
The liquid in the distillation flask will stop boiling due to the pressure buildup.

questions.question: A student wants to prepare a saturated solution of copper sulfate from a dilute solution. How can they achieve this using evaporation?
options: By heating the solution to evaporate some of the solvent, reducing the volume until no more solute can dissolve.
By boiling the solution until all the water is completely gone, leaving only dry powder.
By adding more cold solvent to the solution while stirring rapidly.
By filtering the dilute solution to remove the excess dissolved solute.

questions.question: A student is trying to grow large, well-defined crystals of alum. They set up two beakers: Beaker A is kept in a warm oven at 60°C to evaporate the solvent quickly, while Beaker B is covered with a paper towel and left in a cool room. Which beaker will produce larger crystals and why?
options: Beaker B, because slower evaporation of the solvent allows the particles more time to arrange into a regular lattice.
Beaker A, because rapid evaporation forces the particles together faster to form a larger solid mass.
Beaker A, because higher temperatures provide more energy for crystal growth.
Both beakers will produce identical crystals because crystal size depends only on the solute concentration.

questions.question: A muddy mixture contains fine clay particles suspended in water. Which separation technique should be used to retrieve clean water, and what is the role of the barrier in this process?
options: Filtration, where the solid clay particles are trapped by the filter paper because they cannot pass through its pores.
Crystallisation, where the clay particles reform into crystals as the water is heated.
Decanting, where the water is evaporated to leave the dry clay behind.
Chromatography, where the clay particles travel slower than the water molecules up a paper strip.

questions.question: Before pouring a liquid mixture into a filter paper cone sitting in a glass funnel, a student adds a drop of water to the paper. What is the practical reason for doing this?
options: It helps keep the filter paper cone open and adhered to the funnel sides for easy filtering.
It pre-cleans the filter paper by dissolving any soluble impurities.
It chemically activates the cellulose fibers in the paper to trap smaller particles.
It speeds up the filtration rate by creating a vacuum in the neck of the funnel.

questions.question: You are given a mixture of olive oil and water. If you pour them into a beaker and leave them undisturbed for several minutes, what will you observe and why?
options: They will form two distinct layers with oil on top, because they are immiscible and oil is less dense than water.
They will form two distinct layers with water on top, because they are miscible and water is less dense than oil.
They will remain thoroughly mixed because the molecules of oil and water form strong chemical bonds.
The oil will sink to the bottom as a solid precipitate because it is insoluble in water.

questions.question: A mixture consists of two immiscible liquids, hexane and water. Which method and apparatus are most appropriate to cleanly separate them?
options: Using a separating funnel to drain off the lower layer, leaving the upper layer behind.
Simple distillation, because immiscible liquids cannot be separated physically without boiling.
Filtration, because the larger molecules of hexane will be trapped on the filter paper.
Evaporation, because hexane will evaporate into the air leaving water behind.

questions.question: A mixture is made by thoroughly mixing ethanol and water. If this mixture is left in a sealed flask for several days, what will happen to the liquids?
options: They will remain fully mixed and will not separate into distinct layers because they are miscible.
They will gradually separate into an ethanol layer on top and a water layer on the bottom.
The water will sink to the bottom and the ethanol will crystallise at the surface.
They will undergo a chemical reaction and form an insoluble precipitate at the bottom of the flask.

questions.question: If you have a mixture of two miscible liquids, such as acetone (boiling point 56°C) and water (boiling point 100°C), how can their boiling points be exploited to separate them?
options: By heating the mixture to a temperature where one liquid vaporises while the other remains liquid, then condensing the vapour.
By freezing the mixture so that the liquid with the lower boiling point crystallises first.
By filtering the mixture at a temperature exactly halfway between their boiling points.
By adding a solvent that selectively alters the boiling point of only one of the liquids.

questions.question: A waste bucket contains a mixture of sand, salt, and iron filings. To separate all three substances into pure components, which sequence of techniques should be used?
options: Use a magnet to remove iron, add water to dissolve salt, filter out the sand, and evaporate the water to obtain salt.
Filter the dry mixture to remove sand, use a magnet on the liquid to remove iron, and crystallise the salt.
Heat the mixture to melt the salt, decant the liquid salt from the sand, and use a magnet on the residue.
Distill the mixture to separate the iron and sand, then use chromatography to separate the salt from the water.

questions.question: Rock salt is a mixture of sand, clay, and sodium chloride (salt). What is the correct sequence of steps required to obtain pure salt crystals from rock salt?
options: Dissolve the mixture in water, filter to remove insoluble sand/clay, and then crystallise the salt from the filtrate.
Filter the dry rock salt, dissolve the residue in water, and perform simple distillation.
Heat the rock salt until the salt melts, filter the molten mixture, and leave it to cool.
Perform chromatography on the rock salt solution, then use a magnet to remove any remaining impurities.

questions.question: How can pure water be extracted from a copper sulfate solution so that both the solute and the solvent are recovered?
options: By vaporising the water through heating and then quickly condensing the vapour back into a liquid in a separate container.
By filtering the solution through fine filter paper to trap the dissolved copper sulfate.
By heating the solution to evaporate all the water into the atmosphere, leaving the copper sulfate behind.
By using a separating funnel to drain the copper sulfate layer away from the water layer.

questions.question: What is the fundamental physical principle that allows simple distillation to separate salt from a salt-water solution?
options: The water has a much lower boiling point than the salt, allowing it to turn into gas while the salt remains solid.
The salt particles are larger than water molecules, allowing them to be trapped by the condenser.
The salt is magnetic and is attracted to the metal walls of the distillation flask.
Water is miscible with the salt, which causes the salt to decompose when heated.

questions.question: Why is it critical to run a continuous flow of cold water through the condenser jacket during distillation rather than just filling it once with static cold water?
options: The hot vapour transfers heat to the condenser, so continuous cold water is needed to keep it cold and maintain rapid condensation.
The continuous flow of water creates a pressure difference that sucks the vapour through the tube.
The moving water chemically reacts with the glass to make it more heat-resistant.
The cold water must mix directly with the vapour to dilute the distillate and make it pure.

questions.question: A student distills a mixture of ink and water. At the end of the experiment, they test the liquid collected in the receiving flask (the distillate). What is the nature of this collected liquid?
options: It is pure water, containing no ink pigments or other dissolved solutes.
It is a highly concentrated ink mixture because the pigment vaporised first.
It is a mixture of water and dissolved gases from the condenser jacket.
It is an unsaturated solution of ink because some pigment always passes through the condenser.

questions.question: When separating a mixture of liquids with close boiling points using distillation, why is it beneficial to heat the mixture slowly and gently?
options: It allows for more controlled boiling, ensuring only the component with the lowest boiling point vaporises first.
It prevents the glass flask from cracking under sudden thermal stress.
It ensures that the condenser stays warm enough to prevent the liquids from freezing.
It increases the boiling points of the higher-boiling components so they never vaporise.

questions.question: A forensic scientist needs to analyze a tiny speck of ink recovered from a crime scene to determine if it matches a suspect's pen. Why is chromatography particularly suited for this task?
options: It can be used to separate and analyze minute samples of a substance.
It relies on the ink reacting with the paper to form a permanent record.
It can only analyze large volumes of liquids by evaporating them.
It measures the boiling point of the ink components to identify them.

questions.question: A student performs chromatography on a sample of a food dye and observes that it produces only a single spot on the chromatogram, even when different solvents are used. What does this result indicate about the food dye?
options: The dye is a complex mixture of several different pigments.
The dye is a pure substance.
The dye did not dissolve in any of the solvents.
The dye has reacted chemically with the paper.

questions.question: A chemist is testing a sample of a liquid medication. If the medication is a mixture of active ingredients and additives, what would you expect to see on its chromatogram?
options: No spots at all, as mixtures do not travel up the paper.
A single spot that changes color over time.
Multiple spots at different heights on the chromatogram.
A single large spot that stays at the baseline.

questions.question: How can a student determine if an unknown food dye contains the banned coloring agent "Red 40" using paper chromatography?
options: By seeing if the unknown dye has the exact same boiling point as Red 40.
By running the unknown dye alongside a known sample of Red 40 and comparing if their spots travel the same distance.
By filtering the unknown dye to see if Red 40 is left behind as a residue on the paper.
By measuring the total mass of the chromatogram before and after the run.

questions.question: Why do chemists draw the baseline of a chromatogram in pencil rather than using a standard black ink pen?
options: Pencil lead is more visible through the solvent front than black ink.
Pencil lead is insoluble in water, so it won't dissolve and run up the paper with the sample.
Pencil lead acts as a catalyst to help speed up the separation process.
Ink pens are too heavy and would tear the fragile chromatography paper.

questions.question: A chemical plant needs to separate a mixture of acetone (boiling point 56 degrees Celsius), ethanol (boiling point 78 degrees Celsius), and water (boiling point 100 degrees Celsius). Which technique is most appropriate for this task?
options: Simple distillation
Fractional distillation
Filtration
Paper chromatography

questions.question: During a distillation experiment, the cold water supply to the condenser is accidentally turned off, causing the condenser to warm up. What is the most likely consequence of this?
options: The rate of condensation will increase, producing more pure liquid quickly.
The condenser will become less effective, and more gas will escape into the air.
The boiling point of the liquid in the flask will immediately drop.
The solid solute will start to crystallize inside the condenser tube.

questions.question: How does the process of crystallisation reform a solute as solid crystals from a saturated solution?
options: By filtering the solution through extremely fine mesh paper under high pressure.
By changing conditions, such as cooling the saturated solution, which reduces solubility.
By adding a chemical catalyst that turns the liquid solvent into a solid.
By boiling the solution until all of the solute evaporates into the air.

questions.question: A student wants to grow large, well-defined copper sulfate crystals. What conditions should they use for the crystallisation process?
options: Cool the solution rapidly in an ice bath so the solvent freezes.
Boil the solution vigorously until all the liquid has evaporated.
Allow the solvent to evaporate very slowly at room temperature.
Stir the solution constantly while heating it on a Bunsen burner.

questions.question: A recycling center needs to separate a mixture of shredded metals containing copper, aluminum, brass, and steel. Which property can be directly used to isolate the steel from the other metals?
options: Steel is the only metal in the mixture that is attracted to magnets.
Steel is insoluble in water, while the other metals are soluble.
Steel has a much lower melting point than copper and aluminum.
Steel floats on water, whereas the other metals sink.

questions.question: A student accidentally knocks some sand into a beaker of water. Which method and reasoning should they use to retrieve the dry sand?
options: Distillation, because sand has a lower boiling point than water.
Chromatography, because sand and water will travel at different speeds up paper.
Filtration, because sand is an insoluble solid and will be trapped by the filter paper.
Crystallisation, because evaporating the water will make the sand grow into larger crystals.

questions.question: If oil and water are poured into the same beaker and left to stand, they do not mix. Which statement correctly describes their behavior and arrangement?
options: They are miscible, and the water will float on top of the oil.
They are immiscible, and the less dense oil will float above the water.
They are miscible, and they will form a uniform single-layer solution.
They are immiscible, and they will spontaneously react to form a solid.

questions.question: A mixture contains olive oil and water. Which apparatus would be most efficient to cleanly separate these two immiscible liquids?
options: A Liebig condenser
A separating funnel
A Buchner filtration flask
A chromatography column

questions.question: You mix a sample of ethanol and water together in a flask. If you leave the flask sealed on a shelf for several weeks, what will happen to the mixture?
options: The ethanol and water will separate into two distinct layers because they are miscible.
The ethanol will evaporate to the top of the flask, leaving pure water at the bottom.
The liquids will not separate into layers because miscible liquids remain fully mixed.
The ethanol will crystallize out of the water due to the long waiting period.

questions.question: How can a mixture of two miscible liquids, such as propanol and water, be separated?
options: By filtering the mixture, since one liquid will have larger molecules than the other.
By using their different boiling points to separate them through changes of state.
By using a separating funnel to drain the bottom layer of liquid.
By passing a powerful magnet through the liquid mixture.

questions.question: When choosing a method to separate a mixture of sulfur powder and iron filings, why is magnetic separation chosen over filtration?
options: Because sulfur is soluble in water and iron is not.
Because the specific properties of the substances (iron is magnetic, sulfur is not) determine the best technique.
Because filtration only works for separating two liquids of different densities.
Because magnetic separation is the only method that can separate any solid mixture.

questions.question: A mixture contains sand, salt, and iron filings. Why cannot a single separation technique isolate all three components in their pure forms?
options: Because the mixture contains more than two components, so multiple different techniques must be used in sequence.
Because sand and salt have the exact same chemical properties.
Because iron filings will dissolve if any separation technique is attempted.
Because mixtures with three components can only be separated by chemical reactions.

questions.question: To obtain pure, dry salt from a sample of rock salt (which contains insoluble rock and soluble salt), what is the correct sequence of steps?
options: Filtration, then crystallisation, then dissolving in water.
Dissolving in water (making a solution), then filtration, then crystallisation.
Simple distillation, then magnetic separation, then chromatography.
Evaporation to dryness, then decanting, then manual sorting.

questions.question: Why is simple distillation effective at separating pure water from a salty water solution?
options: Because salt and water have different boiling points, allowing water to vaporize while salt remains behind.
Because salt is lighter than water and will evaporate first at lower temperatures.
Because water reacts chemically with the glass of the flask to leave salt behind.
Because the filter paper in the distillation apparatus traps the dissolved salt.

questions.question: Why is it important to continuously run cold water through the outer sleeve of a Liebig condenser during distillation?
options: To keep the condenser cold, which speeds up the rate of condensation of the vapor.
To wash away any impurities that might build up on the outside of the glass.
To increase the pressure inside the distillation flask so the liquid boils faster.
To prevent the glass from melting due to the high temperature of the flame.
